Hi Mike — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can pull together pricing options that match your unit economics.

Call recap (30m):
- Use case: clinical triage + care coordination summaries (short prompts, average response ~420 tokens).
- Expected traffic profile: bursty during business hours, ~20–25% peak hour concentration.
- Key asks today: a realistic per-1M token target that gets you comfortable to pilot, and whether procurement will accept staged commit windows (3/6 months).

Can you confirm two quick items so I can finalize the quote:
1) Estimated range of monthly tokens you expect in month 1–6 (min / expected / max).
2) Ballpark budget range for inference (monthly) or a target $/1M tokens you want to aim for.

To help, we ran a quick host comparison on the call. High-level: OpenAI/Anthropic public pricing is a useful reference, but open-model hosts (self-host / other vendors) vary widely by quantization profile, caching, and commit. I attached a short snapshot and an initial 3-tier price worksheet — will refine after your numbers.

Proposed next steps:
- You send the volume/budget numbers by EOD tomorrow.
- We return 2 tailored pricing options (pilot + committed) and a recommended rollout that balances latency and unit cost.
- If procurement is ready, we can include a short SOW for a 3-month pilot.

Attachments: Redwood_price_options_3-tier.xlsx (spreadsheet), host_comparison_snapshot.png (slide).

Thanks — Karthik

Mike — thanks for the clarity, very helpful. I pulled together a short apples-to-apples note (high level) to help procurement/finance and attached the updated worksheet. Key signals:

Apples-to-apples drivers (short):
- Model baseline: same family / sequence length (~420 tokens avg) — tokenization overhead assumed equal.
- OpenAI/Anthropic: public list prices for hosted endpoints are typically higher on per-token but include managed infra, autoscaled availability, and standard SLAs. They rarely publish volume discounts below certain commit thresholds.
- Open-model hosts / self-host: can be materially cheaper at high volume if you run aggressive quantization + long-lived KV cache, but operational overhead + burst handling is the kicker.
- Redwood: we can route by policy and apply prefix/KV cache + batching optimizations and model quantization profiles to reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs. That means for your profile (bursty business hours + short prompts) we usually hit better-than-host unit economics with modest commits because caching reduces repeated token spend.

Initial benchmark sketch (per 1M tokens, net of caching assumptions — rough ranges):
- OpenAI (hosted, list): $320 — $400 per 1M (no volume discount applied)
- Anthropic (hosted, list): $300 — $380 per 1M
- Typical open-model host (managed): $160 — $260 per 1M (depends on quantization and KV cache hit rate)
- Redwood (proposed ranges depending on commit & features): $140 — $220 per 1M

Concrete proposal for pilot:
- 3-month committed pilot (3M tokens/month floor): $180 per 1M, with a monthly overage rate of $210 per 1M. Includes SOC2 evidence package and 4-hour support response for P1 during pilot.
- 6-month commit (6M tokens/month floor): $160 per 1M, overage $190 per 1M, includes 24/7 escalation access and custom quantization profiling.

I'll attach the worksheet (Redwood_price_options_3-tier.xlsx) which breaks down assumptions (cache hit %, avg seq len, expected batching uplift). Laura — can you validate the channel for providing SOC2 artifacts and confirm timelines?

If these look OK, next step is a short procurement call with our Solutions Engineer (15–20m) to walk through the pilot SOW and the SOC2 checklist. Candidate times: Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks — Karthik
